payload.recallText: I grew up in Providence Rhode Island and lived close to the Kennedys. We were like relatives. One time after Thanksgiving dinner driving home from grandma's house we were listening to the radio and they were talking about the tenth anniversary of the JFK assassination and I started to cry and my sister told my father I was crying and he pulled the car over and turned around and told me to never be ashamed of crying for that man.  Every year in the seventies my four aunts would take me and my two cousins to a rented beach house and my aunts would all grab their beach chairs and apply sunscreen on their feet and backs of necks and hands and instead of facing the water they would face their chairs to spy on the Kennedys.  They would pay attention to every move the Kennedy's were making. While my aunts were paying attention to the Kennedys my cousins and I went in the water and we got swept out in the water and our aunts looked so far away. All of a sudden a powerboat pulls up with David and Michael Kennedy and they saved us and pulled us on the boat. On the way back to shore we could see our aunts were going to give it to us and they started yelling at us and yelling out our addresses.
